questions.question: What type of variation is characterized by features that fall into distinct, separate categories with no intermediates?
options: Continuous variation
Discontinuous variation
Environmental variation
Graduated variation

questions.question: Which statement best describes a feature that shows continuous variation?
options: It can only be grouped into distinct, non-overlapping categories.
It can take any value within a specific range.
It is entirely unaffected by environmental factors.
It is controlled by only a single gene with two alleles.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of human features correctly lists one discontinuous feature followed by one continuous feature?
options: Blood group and eye colour
Height and body mass
Blood group and height
Lobeless ears and ability to roll tongue

questions.question: Which type of chart is most appropriate for displaying continuous data, such as the heights of 100 oak trees?
options: Bar chart
Pie chart
Histogram
Pictogram

questions.question: When plotting a histogram to show continuous variation in human body mass, how should the data on the horizontal axis (x-axis) be structured?
options: In discrete categories with spaces between bars
In continuous, adjacent intervals or ranges
As individual names of the participants
As percentages of the total population

questions.question: In a normal distribution histogram representing the heights of adult humans, what shape does the data typically form?
options: A flat, horizontal straight line
A bell-shaped curve with most people near the average
An upward sloping diagonal line from left to right
Two separate, isolated peaks with nothing in the middle

questions.question: Why do features like human skin colour or height show continuous variation rather than discontinuous variation?
options: They are controlled by a single gene and unaffected by the environment.
They are influenced by multiple genes as well as environmental and lifestyle factors.
They are only affected by lifestyle choices and have no genetic basis.
They are determined solely by the climate in which a person lives.

questions.question: Why is a bar chart with gaps between the columns used to display data for discontinuous variation?
options: To show that the data can take any value within a range
To represent the continuous flow of the categories
To emphasize that the categories are distinct and separate
To indicate that the values are measured on a continuous scale

questions.question: When plotting blood groups (A, B, AB, O) on a bar chart, how should the bars be drawn?
options: Touching each other to show a continuous range
With equal gaps between them to show distinct categories
As a single line connecting all data points
As a circular pie slice for each blood group

questions.question: If you look at a bar chart showing the frequency of different tongue-rolling abilities in a classroom, what does each individual bar represent?
options: A range of different tongue lengths
The percentage of students of different heights
A distinct, separate category of tongue-rolling ability
The average age of students who can roll their tongues

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the causes of discontinuous variation in humans, such as having hitchhiker's thumb?
options: It is heavily influenced by diet and daily exercise.
It usually has only a genetic cause and is unaffected by lifestyle.
It changes gradually throughout an individual's life due to environmental factors.
It is caused entirely by the geographic location where a person is raised.

questions.question: Why do human siblings often look similar to each other and to their parents, but are not identical?
options: They inherit all their features from only one parent.
They inherit a unique mix of genetic features from both parents.
They are raised in completely different environments.
They copy each other's physical appearance as they grow up.

questions.question: How are inherited features, such as natural eye colour, passed from parents to their offspring?
options: Through the transmission of DNA during reproduction
Through learned behaviours in early childhood
Through nutrients shared in the environment
Through physical contact after birth

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a feature in an organism that is directly changed by its lifestyle or environment?
options: An individual's blood group
The presence of a scar from an injury
The natural colour of a person's eyes
The biological sex of a mammal

questions.question: When comparing a group of domestic dogs and a group of domestic cats, how do the differences between these two species compare to the differences within the dog species itself?
options: Differences within the dog species are much greater than between dogs and cats.
Differences between the species are equal to the differences within the dog species.
Differences between the species are greater than differences within the species.
There are no measurable differences between dogs and cats.

questions.question: What scientific term is used to describe the differences in features between individuals of the same species?
options: Classification
Variation
Adaptation
Inheritance

questions.question: Which of the following variations is caused solely by environmental factors and has no genetic basis?
options: Having a tattoo on your arm
Having naturally curly hair
Having blue eyes
Having Type O blood

questions.question: Which variation in humans is determined solely by inherited genetic information and cannot be changed by lifestyle?
options: Body mass
ABO blood group
Language spoken
Muscle strength

questions.question: Human body mass is a feature that is determined by which of the following?
options: Only genetic information passed from parents
Only the amount of daily exercise a person gets
A combination of genetic factors and environmental/lifestyle factors
Only the altitude of the environment where a person lives
